## Load packages

`pROC` is called with `::`.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, mixOmics, dplyr, tidyr, tibble, purrr, ggplot2, patchwork, writexl)
here::i_am("07_Multivariate/02_splsda/a_script/02_splsda.qmd")
```

## Read proteins

```{r read}
stage <- here("07_Multivariate", "02_splsda")
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
targets <- proteins$targets
gene_of <- set_names(proteins$genes$Genes, rownames(proteins))
dim(proteins$E)
```

## Build the four comparisons

Sparse PLS-DA (Lê Cao et al. 2011, doi:10.1186/1471-2105-12-253) builds a score from a weighted
sum of a few proteins, chosen to separate two groups. Each comparison here takes two samples per
participant, and `multilevel = participant` subtracts each participant's mean first (Liquet et
al. 2012), so the score compares a person's two samples with each other:

- training in each arm: a leg's sample before training (T1) against after (T2);
- BFR against HLRT on change: each leg's T2 minus T1, one leg against the other;
- BFR against HLRT after training: the two legs' T2 samples.

Participants without both samples a comparison needs drop out of that comparison. A two-factor
multilevel design on all four samples is not used: with one sample per participant, leg and time,
its decomposition is computed from the class labels themselves.

```{r comparisons}
legs <- targets |>
  mutate(leg_id = paste(participant, leg, sep = "_")) |>
  select(leg_id, participant, treatment, timepoint, sample_id) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = sample_id) |>
  drop_na(T1, T2)

training <- function(arm) {
  arm_legs <- filter(legs, treatment == arm)
  list(
    x = t(proteins$E[, c(arm_legs$T1, arm_legs$T2)]),
    y = factor(rep(c("T1", "T2"), each = nrow(arm_legs))),
    participant = rep(arm_legs$participant, 2)
  )
}

paired_legs <- legs |> filter(n() == 2, .by = participant)
change <- t(proteins$E[, paired_legs$T2] - proteins$E[, paired_legs$T1])
rownames(change) <- paired_legs$leg_id
post <- targets |> filter(timepoint == "T2") |> filter(n() == 2, .by = participant)

comparisons <- list(
  training_bfr = training("BFR"),
  training_hlrt = training("HLRT"),
  arms_change = list(
    x = change, y = factor(paired_legs$treatment, c("HLRT", "BFR")),
    participant = paired_legs$participant
  ),
  arms_post = list(
    x = t(proteins$E[, post$sample_id]), y = factor(post$treatment, c("HLRT", "BFR")),
    participant = post$participant
  )
)
comparison_labels <- c(
  training_bfr = "Training, BFR leg: T1 vs T2",
  training_hlrt = "Training, HLRT leg: T1 vs T2",
  arms_change = "BFR vs HLRT, training change",
  arms_post = "BFR vs HLRT, after training"
)
map(comparisons, \(cmp) table(cmp$y))
```

## Tune, fit and cross-validate

For each comparison, `tune.splsda()` tries panels of 5 to 1,000 proteins on each of two
components and keeps the size with the lowest balanced error rate (BER, the mean of the two
groups' error rates; 0.5 is chance). Cross-validation is 5-fold, repeated 50 times, and folds hold
out whole participants. `splsda()` then fits the chosen panel on everyone, and `perf()` reruns the
same cross-validation on that model to give the BER under each of the package's three
classification rules and the cross-validated AUC. The panel size was chosen on the same data, so
these error rates are somewhat optimistic; there is no permutation reference. Proteins are scaled
to unit variance (the default).

```{r fit}
keep_grid <- c(5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000)
fit_splsda <- function(cmp) {
  tuned <- tune.splsda(
    cmp$x, cmp$y, ncomp = 2, test.keepX = keep_grid, multilevel = cmp$participant,
    validation = "Mfold", folds = 5, nrepeat = 50, dist = "max.dist", measure = "BER",
    seed = 2026
  )
  model <- splsda(cmp$x, cmp$y, ncomp = 2, keepX = tuned$choice.keepX,
    multilevel = cmp$participant)
  performance <- perf(model, validation = "Mfold", folds = 5, nrepeat = 50, dist = "all",
    auc = TRUE, seed = 2026)
  list(tuned = tuned, model = model, performance = performance)
}
fits <- map(comparisons, fit_splsda)
```

## Error and AUC

One row per comparison and component: panel size, the tuning BER at that size, `perf()`'s mean
BER under each rule, and the cross-validated AUC.

```{r models}
model_summary <- imap(fits, function(fit, name) {
  ber <- fit$performance$error.rate$BER
  ber_sd <- fit$performance$error.rate.sd$BER
  tibble(
    comparison = name,
    n_participants = n_distinct(comparisons[[name]]$participant),
    n_samples = nrow(comparisons[[name]]$x),
    component = 1:2,
    keep_x = unname(fit$tuned$choice.keepX),
    tune_ber = map2_dbl(keep_x, component, \(k, h) fit$tuned$error.rate[as.character(k), h]),
    ber_max = ber[, "max.dist"],
    ber_max_sd = ber_sd[, "max.dist"],
    ber_centroids = ber[, "centroids.dist"],
    ber_mahalanobis = ber[, "mahalanobis.dist"],
    auc = map_dbl(fit$performance$auc, "AUC.mean"),
    auc_sd = map_dbl(fit$performance$auc, "AUC.sd")
  )
}) |>
  list_rbind()
model_summary |> mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

## Panels

Every protein the final model selects, with its loading (its weight in the component score; the
sign gives the direction) and its stability, the share of the 250 cross-validation refits that
also selected it.

```{r panels}
panels <- imap(fits, function(fit, name) {
  map(1:2, function(h) {
    loading <- fit$model$loadings$X[, h]
    stable <- fit$performance$features$stable[[h]]
    tibble(protein = names(loading), loading = unname(loading)) |>
      filter(loading != 0) |>
      mutate(
        comparison = name, component = h, gene = gene_of[protein],
        stability = coalesce(as.numeric(stable[protein]), 0), .before = protein
      ) |>
      arrange(desc(abs(loading)))
  }) |>
    list_rbind()
}) |>
  list_rbind()
panels |> summarise(proteins = n(), stable_80 = sum(stability >= 0.8),
  .by = c(comparison, component))
```

## Figures

One page per comparison:

- the samples on the two component scores, with a line joining each participant's two samples;
- the ROC curve of each of the 50 cross-validation repeats, built from component 1's held-out
  predictions;
- the 25 largest loadings on each component, shaded by stability.

```{r figures}
#| fig-height: 10
group_colours <- c(T1 = "grey55", T2 = "#009E73", HLRT = "#0072B2", BFR = "#D55E00")

score_plot <- function(fit, cmp) {
  as_tibble(fit$model$variates$X, rownames = "sample") |>
    mutate(group = cmp$y, participant = cmp$participant) |>
    ggplot(aes(comp1, comp2, colour = group)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = participant), colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_point(size = 1.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = group_colours) +
    labs(x = "Component 1", y = "Component 2", colour = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 8)
}

roc_plot <- function(fit, cmp) {
  predicted <- fit$performance$predict$comp1
  curves <- map(seq_len(dim(predicted)[3]), function(r) {
    roc <- pROC::roc(cmp$y, predicted[, 2, r], levels = levels(cmp$y), direction = "<",
      quiet = TRUE)
    tibble(repeat_id = r, specificity = roc$specificities, sensitivity = roc$sensitivities)
  }) |>
    list_rbind()
  auc <- fit$performance$auc$comp1
  ggplot(curves, aes(1 - specificity, sensitivity, group = repeat_id)) +
    geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey70") +
    geom_step(alpha = 0.15, direction = "vh") +
    annotate("text", x = 0.62, y = 0.08, size = 2.8,
      label = sprintf("CV AUC %.2f ± %.2f", auc[["AUC.mean"]], auc[["AUC.sd"]])) +
    coord_equal() +
    labs(x = "1 − specificity", y = "Sensitivity") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 8)
}

loading_plot <- function(name, h) {
  panels |>
    filter(comparison == name, component == h) |>
    slice_max(abs(loading), n = 25, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    ggplot(aes(loading, reorder(gene, loading), fill = stability)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey85", high = "grey15", limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = paste("Component", h, "loading"), y = NULL, fill = "Stability") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 7)
}

pages <- imap(fits, function(fit, name) {
  headline <- filter(model_summary, comparison == name, component == 1)
  (score_plot(fit, comparisons[[name]]) | roc_plot(fit, comparisons[[name]])) /
    (loading_plot(name, 1) | loading_plot(name, 2)) +
    plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1.4), guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(
      title = comparison_labels[[name]],
      subtitle = sprintf("%d participants; component 1: %d proteins, CV BER %.2f",
        headline$n_participants, headline$keep_x, headline$ber_max)
    )
})
pages[[1]]

pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", "02_splsda.pdf"), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
walk(pages, print)
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Save results

```{r write}
write_xlsx(
  list(
    models = model_summary,
    panels = panels,
    scores = imap(fits, function(fit, name) {
      as_tibble(fit$model$variates$X, rownames = "sample") |>
        mutate(comparison = name, participant = comparisons[[name]]$participant,
          group = as.character(comparisons[[name]]$y), .before = 1)
    }) |>
      list_rbind()
  ),
  file.path(stage, "c_data", "02_splsda.xlsx")
)
```
